A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same MemoryBench study with readable main text and complete Appendix A. All 23 tables and 14 figures can be matched; formatting differences do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original benchmark experiments, feedback and robustness analyses, and a 200-task human evaluation of simulated feedback (Appendices A.2.5 and A.3).

after.justification: v7 retains the original benchmark experiments, human evaluation, and supplementary empirical analyses reported in v5.

M1.justification: The Task Provider, User Simulator, Performance Monitor, hybrid feedback simulation, and memory-handling procedures remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both use the same 11 source datasets, three domains, two languages, and four input/output task categories. MemoryBench-Full was already described but excluded from reported experiments in v5 Appendix A.3.1; this remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The same Vanilla, four RAG variants, A-Mem, Mem0, and MemoryOS comparisons remain, including unchanged experiment-specific exclusions. SFT already appears in the action-feedback comparison in Table 20 of both versions.

E3.justification: Sampling, 4:1 training/test splits, evaluation metrics and normalization, model backbones, feedback-turn limits, and on-policy/off-policy procedures match. The appendix reports the same training and testing settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the human feedback validation, feedback/no-feedback comparisons, stepwise learning analyses, timing investigation, noisy-action tests, backbone comparisons, and legal case study. No analysis or tested question is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 13–14 retain standard deviations across test data, and Table 7 retains Fleiss' kappa. Seed information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged; no additional repeated-run or confidence reporting appears.

E6.justification: Matched numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 10 retains Legal-domain normalized scores of 0.5011 for BM25-M and 0.4684 for A-Mem. Appendix feedback, robustness, timing, and case-study results also match.

T1.justification: Section 2.1's formalization of continual learning and Appendix A.2.3's assumptions and action-probability equations remain unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The benchmark contributions and central effectiveness/efficiency claims remain unchanged. The conclusion omits a repeated feedback-quality assurance, but the underlying claim remains in Sections 2.4 and 3.3 and Appendix A.2.5; it is not withdrawn from the paper.

C2.justification: v7's conclusion explicitly acknowledges that MemoryBench's simulation framework may introduce systematic evaluation biases. This adds a qualification to v5's positive feedback-quality summary, while retaining the existing interpretations and limitation analyses.

D1.justification: v7 adds a project-website address and changes the documented code repository from LittleDinoC/MemoryBench to THUIR/MemoryBench. MemoryBench-Full access was already disclosed in v5 Appendix A.3.1. Technical implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Removing the URL from the LexEval bibliography entry does not remove that citation or alter its relationship to MemoryBench.

P1.justification: v7 edits the conclusion, adds a front-page resource block, replaces the preprint notice with ICML proceedings information, and removes the Impact Statement's section number. Overall section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from page 7 to page 8, and text and appendix prompt boxes reflow. The front-page resource block changes the opening layout. All figures and tables retain their content and display structures.

improvement.justification: The conclusion makes potential simulation bias more explicit, and the front-page resource block makes access information easier to find. These provide modest transparency and usability gains. The methods, empirical evidence, and appendix analyses remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
